rationale: Multipart parsing previously returned maps missing file or fileName. It now requires both entries and throws when either is absent.
Concurrent permission calculation could overwrite permissions reset after parent group discovery. Synchronization now prevents that stale overwrite so parent group access remains available.
Adapter requests previously defaulted Content-Type to the top-level application token. They now default to application/json and include an Accept header defaulting to all media types.
Only LDAP configuration key constants are added. No request handling or use of these constants is introduced.

Namespace normalization now reapplies application tracking metadata to namespaced resources lacking a namespace as well as malformed cluster resources. Returned target state and comparison error messages can differ.
Cleanup task batching reads configuration through the realm context instead of the enclosing call context. The shown change affects internal batch sizing rather than API data or cleanup targets.
An empty configured server path becomes a slash. The supplied validator does not show whether consumers distinguish these paths in HTTP routing or generated URLs.
Endpoint descriptors now build URLs using the configured prefix and callback address and include configurable subprotocol information. Advertised endpoint URLs can change for existing configurations.
Origins beginning with the loopback IPv4 HTTP prefix now receive the CORS headers previously granted only to localhost by this special case.
Cancellation previously directly marked reusable callers cancelled after their children. It now rereads callers with children and preserves the status produced by child aggregation.
Password policy failures now return structured validation errors for minimum length and identifier similarity and breach counts instead of the previous generic errors.
After sending method-not-allowed for an unknown HTTP method the handler now marks the request handled. Subsequent handlers can no longer replace that response through the unhandled path.
Display-name validation moves from the controller to a permission helper receiving a new flag. The helper implementation is absent so equivalence or changed acceptance cannot be established.
segmentID previously tracked the last visited segment even without a selected variant. It now changes only when a segment selects a variant and otherwise remains zero.
Controller changes are indentation and suppression-comment removal. Model imports are reordered. Request processing and response construction remain the same.
The path and build validation limits increase from 20 to 120 characters. Values between 21 and 120 characters can now pass these constraints.
New test router constructors reuse existing router factories. The production router implementation and prefix behavior are unchanged.
Search permissions now use the MSAL home account identifier instead of the former unique identifier. Silent refresh failures also retain valid sessions instead of propagating refresh exceptions.

Transaction helpers change nested-transaction handling while shown AutoTx callers retain equivalent WithTx behavior. The nested TxContext implementation is redacted and HTTP callers of changed semantics are unavailable.
Only an import switches packages. The session deletion handler body is unchanged.
Question pages using short-ID permalinks now generate a canonical URL without the title slug. Previously only the ordinary question-ID permalink mode omitted the slug.
Seven vulnerability count columns are added to the persistence report model. No supplied handler or conversion establishes whether they change an HTTP response or API-visible state.
The wallet response parameter is renamed and its interface becomes a functional interface. Lookup and response selection remain identical.
Stopping scan-all previously stopped existing execution tasks while artifact enumeration could continue launching scans. A cached stop flag now terminates enumeration and cancels its iterator.
Startup failure handling now distinguishes required web contexts from optional ones. The supplied code does not establish a changed completed HTTP response for a running service.
Flow initialization adds a deprecation logger invocation. No access policy enforcement or HTTP handling is changed.
Process updates now prefill configuration from the existing process before binding JSON. Omitted fields retain stored values instead of receiving the previous fresh defaults.

Artifact operations switch file-manager methods and upload bookkeeping. The implementations of the old and new storage operations are absent so their externally visible equivalence cannot be determined.
The access DTO gains an address-protection access list record component. Serialized DTO responses can now include this additional field.
Three package model classes are introduced without any changed handler or integration using them. Existing HTTP execution is not changed by the shown additions.
Struct tags add documentation and read-only schema metadata. JSON field names and the shown model operations and permission validation remain unchanged.
Project creation now trims names and rejects names shorter than the minimum after trimming. Project name replacement also strips surrounding whitespace before storage.
A hidden trusted flag replaces the separate trusted-location subtype. Client location updates remain ignored and server-created trusted location updates still apply.
Page zero now normalizes to page one. Negative page numbers and sizes are normalized instead of throwing assertion errors.
DNS timeout cancellation gains a cause but resolver errors are still discarded. The same IP ranges are checked and the same validation results are returned.
Diagnostics are stored in a field and passed to the transaction workspace constructor. The shown validation and catalog operations otherwise remain unchanged.
Kafka operations now use a bounded dedicated executor. Requests rejected when its pool and queue are full receive a 503 overload error instead of being submitted to the previous executor.
Charge selection changes in a business-event serializer. The supplied code shows event output rather than an HTTP response or API-visible stored-state mutation.
Preview generation no longer returns nil solely because cache operations fail. Cache read failures allow rendering and cache write failures leave the generated preview available.
A primarySpec field is added to the YAML registry interchange model. No HTTP serialization or operation using this model is changed in the supplied files.
Strict-mode batch checks with unknown membership and a limitation now include the limitation in the error field. Previously that field was empty unless an explicit error existed.
The accepted settings enum replaces the footer-links key with the sidebar-links key. Requests using the removed enum value no longer deserialize as before.
Setting compatibility to NONE now stores an explicit rule instead of deleting it. Missing rules now use configured default global compatibility rather than always reporting NONE.
Submodel element creation still delegates the same mutation. Its Kafka event now receives the full child path rather than the parent path; no HTTP output change is shown.
The protocol binding bean gains a routingKey property and accessors. Binding representations can now include the additional optional property.
Organization domain and identity-provider link lookups gain cache support. The shown changes preserve the values returned for existing organizations and links.
A two-factor passkey response previously fell through into the one-factor response handler and could lose its redirect. It now returns immediately after constructing the two-factor response.
The helper classifies the API root differently and adds root-or-nested matching. Its consumers are not supplied so an effect on responses versus logging alone cannot be determined.
Only comments in contract-test API stubs are reformatted. Executable behavior is unchanged.
The existing protected-resource metadata enablement expression moves into an APISpec helper. Its precedence and fallback conditions remain identical.
The device endpoint depends on a session repository interface instead of its previous specialized type. No repository calls or HTTP behavior are modified.
Configuration validation adds scrypt variant checks and renames internal identifiers. The shown code validates startup configuration rather than HTTP request inputs.
An audit extension persistence model is added and registered. No supplied request handler reads or writes it and no existing response model changes.
Two persistence fetch groups and their enum names are removed. Component fields and serialization are unchanged and no changed HTTP data selection is shown.
A link passed to the email notification service gains a slash. The shown change affects email content rather than an HTTP outcome or API-visible state.
Recent time-series queries by explicit IDs now pass the office to the DAO. Previously those queries omitted office scoping and could return values from another office.
Wallet responses now accept a response form field containing a signed JARM JWT and verify it before processing. Previously only direct-post form fields were interpreted.
Payment search logging redacts personal fields and switch syntax is modernized. Status selection and response headers and entities remain the same.
Comment pagination now decodes the comment identifier from short form before lookup. Previously only the object identifier was decoded.
Entitlements lacking purchase data now produce a null billing-provider identifier instead of dereference failures. Azure purchase records with null contract lists now use an empty plan identifier.
Visitor callback types gain a context parameter. No request handling or callback implementation behavior changes are shown.
Project PATCH previously parsed a project body for update. It now requires name and office query parameters and performs a rename using the path name.

The before method redeclares pagination locals and combines string parameters with numeric expressions. The patch removes these inconsistent declarations but a runnable before HTTP behavior cannot be established.
Repository interfaces gain a count method and a job-target repository type. No implementation or operation invokes new behavior in the supplied changes.
The after files contain unresolved merge markers around model fields and dependency injection. A definite deployed HTTP representation cannot be inferred from this invalid source snapshot.
A request-specific JARM JWKS endpoint is registered. It returns public ephemeral keys for eligible presentations and explicit not-found or bad-request responses for other states.
Only deprecation documentation changes. Kafka configuration fields and methods remain identical.
The accept header remains readable from external requests but is no longer marked for publication to external response headers.
The user-update permission function moves to a separate file with local variable renaming. Compared fields and permission checks remain the same.
An unknown commit used as the list base now follows not-found error mapping. Previously every failure to load that commit returned an internal-server-error response.
Omitting channel on video playlists or segments now selects channel one. Previously the unannotated primitive query parameter defaulted to zero.
Logging switches from SLF4J to Log4j and logger references are renamed. The HTTP branches and response construction are unchanged.
Expired sessions now attempt silent token renewal instead of immediately failing refresh. Failed renewals are throttled and results already expired are not installed.
A non-HTTPS return URL error for a live account now maps to 422 with code P0920. Previously it fell through to the generic connector error mapping.
Validation field messages now gain a trailing period when absent and an uppercase first character. Previously messages were returned without this normalization.

Artifact and version creation now receive the authenticated principal as owner. Internal artifact-update methods also gain write-authorization interception instead of remaining private unannotated helpers.
Adding loan charges previously left disbursement charges unchanged. Fee charges now accumulate into the amount used to construct disbursement schedule data.
DOI-setting updates replace explicit writer-or-admin-or-curator authorization with checkCanWrite. That inherited helper is absent so whether the authorized caller set changes cannot be established.
Aggregate source information gains an annotationSourcesInfo list property with source-version records. Existing source information fields remain available.
Only contract-test stubs are refactored and an empty subscription-search response helper is added. Production HTTP request processing is unchanged.
Repository import previously returned 201 for empty files and unsupported types and caught import failures. It now returns 400 for empty files and 415 for unsupported types and 500 for failures.
A validation log includes the throwable class through toString instead of only its message. No returned validation result changes.
YAML interchange metadata can omit empty values and new list and project interchange types are added. No HTTP handler or wire representation is changed in the supplied files.
Deleting the last unfrozen workflow version now unpublishes a published workflow. Other deletions now refresh the public index instead of leaving its previous entry unchanged.
Modifier order and redundant punctuation are cleaned up and local variables become final. JSON configuration and resource loading behavior remain identical.
Success and error paths now record access logs when configured. Returned proxy responses and error responses remain unchanged.
Only lint-suppression comments are added to response construction. All returned fields retain the same values.

V2 plan security configuration now uses a named serialization mapper. Neither the mapper implementation nor the generated previous mapping is supplied so the actual response type change cannot be verified.
Connection validation now rejects invalid diversion response types and malformed or self-directed connection IDs. Diversion targets with configured topics are also newly rejected.
Controller constraints switch from javax to jakarta validation annotations. The supplied files do not establish which validation provider was active before and whether request enforcement changes.

The patch repairs transaction-aware duplicate counting and constructor arguments. The before source calls a count signature absent from the supplied class so its running HTTP behavior cannot be established.
Login and token-exchange trace events gain corrected subject and request context. The HTTP error and redirect responses remain unchanged.

Internal Gitspace requests now use code_repo_ref instead of code_repo_url for repository lookup. Creation dereferences the new pointer even when omitted and actions explicitly reject a missing reference.
Only the password validator cache dependency import switches to its version-two path. Validation rules and the shown cache calls are unchanged.
Only a test for query character acceptance is added. Production request parsing is unchanged.
A position attribute key constant is added without assigning that attribute or changing any serializer or handler.
Endpoint-tracking conversion helpers are introduced without changed call sites invoking them. The shown addition alone does not change a request path or response.
A documentation spelling error is corrected. Executable code is unchanged.
Available commands selected for a device are now ordered by description before type filtering. Previously the database query specified no order.
Push and API reference or content updates no longer run merge-queue branch-update verification. Updates previously rejected solely by that check can now proceed.
Transaction execution and callback methods are renamed and endpoint-service call sites follow the rename. Transaction bodies remain the same.
Placeholder OAuth authorization and OIDC login responses change from 200 success to 405 failure. The OAuth redirect route is replaced by userinfo and an OIDC redirect route is added.

Revision-path comparison now also runs without automated sync and for directory sources. Failures from this newly reached comparison call can produce application comparison errors where manifest generation previously proceeded directly.

Implicit subscription previously skipped entities already covered by an inherited subscription. It now creates an own subscription so later unsubscribing from the parent leaves the child subscription active.
Snapshot requests without an explicit limit previously had no limit applied here. They now use a configured positive default and can return fewer snapshots.

Installation recommendations now receive the triggering account rather than the authenticated webhook account. The recommendation helper is absent so an effect visible through HTTP cannot be established.
Theme routes switch to a resolver from another package and the former implementation is deleted. The replacement implementation is absent so template-selection equivalence cannot be verified.
A missing widget session registry is now replaced with a new registry. Previously it returned uptime-only data. The supplied files do not show the new registry's collector behavior.
Only the imported database library fork changes. No OAuth handler logic or responses are modified in the provided source.
TimeoutException no longer counts as an interruption in the shared helper. No helper callers are supplied to establish whether HTTP errors or only internal cleanup behavior changes.
When container metadata configuration is present the admin HTTP server now exposes a Prometheus metrics servlet at /metrics. Previously this servlet was not registered.
Passkey credential imports now reject missing user handles and empty resulting credentials with bad-request errors. Previously these cases reached credential storage.
Grace-period fields are added only to the Swagger documentation model. No actual loan request parser or response model changes.
The patch-all controller dependency changes to an asynchronous service type. Its implementation is absent so response timing alone versus changed errors or persistence behavior cannot be determined.
Missing products in review operations change from 400 to 404. Specific exception handlers gain priority and malformed-input exceptions bypass the global 500 handler.
The dry-run endpoint no longer opens a controller transaction. The called service is absent so identical dry-run behavior versus changed persistence failures or visibility cannot be established.

Group listing gains a subGroupsCount option defaulting to true. Brief subgroup responses previously skipped count population but now include counts by default and clients can explicitly suppress them.
Imported HTTP examples now copy dispatch criteria onto the response object before constructing the exchange. Previously those imported responses lacked this dispatch selection metadata.
Bridge representations gain optional websocketConfiguration details. Bridge create and update conversion also preserves an enabled websocket transport configuration instead of omitting it.

Consumer endpoint and timestamp registries are now concurrent and close callbacks remove both entries. Cleanup no longer mutates a HashMap iterator through close callbacks and can finish removing stale consumers.
Variant annotation beans gain an errorMessage property and accessors. Serialized annotation responses can now include the additional field.
Lombok generates the same page-revision accessors and adds constructors and a builder. New audit event enum values have no changed producer in the supplied files.
Concurrent submodel mutations now share a lock. Duplicate checks and additions and replacement sequences are serialized instead of racing and potentially storing duplicate or inconsistent elements.
Kafka configuration renames localServerId to messageKey with compatibility accessors. Kafka records retain the same configured key and event body; no HTTP representation is changed.
Policy-condition values no longer have a 255-character maximum. Expression subjects and a violation-type property are also supported with expression-specific validation errors.
Certificate attribute provider types are added without integration into an existing HTTP processor. No changed caller uses the provider in the supplied production changes.

Empty privilege-set equality and containsAll and array conversion semantics change. No authorization caller is supplied to show whether any request decision or HTTP response depends on those operations.
The exception copies its product-ID list and extracts message construction into a helper. For the supplied IDs its immediate error message and identifier values remain identical.

Hook resources previously always received an application label. They now use configured annotation or label tracking and installation metadata with label truncation when annotation-plus-label tracking is selected.
Skipped debug objects were already excluded from responses by the same flags. Rollout now uses the preformatted flag identifier instead of formatting it during evaluation.
Location-level listing gains an optional include-aliases query flag and an aliases response collection. Empty aliases are omitted and the flag defaults to false.
Reload adds an informational log identifying the configuration path. No configuration processing or HTTP output changes.
Vision model configuration gains Run and scheduling helpers. Their invocation and HTTP exposure are not supplied so a request outcome change cannot be established from this addition alone.
Variant annotation beans gain a genomicLocationExplanation property and accessors. Serialized annotation responses can now include the additional field.
A helper can add vulnerability aliases to a finding but no changed constructor or caller invokes it. Existing finding serialization is unchanged unless that new helper is used.
Schema field validation no longer premarks the initial column identifier as used. A field with that identifier no longer triggers a duplicate-ID error solely because of the sentinel.
